thread.title: Hedge-fund luminary Einhorn says he’s ‘never underperformed like this’

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Hedge-fund luminary Einhorn says he’s ‘never underperformed like this’
text:
Hedge-fund manager David Einhorn just posted his worst January performance in about 18 years, according to news reports. 
Here’s how he described his recent results during a Wednesday morning conference call with investors in Greenlight Capital Re Ltd.: 
“While we’ve never underperformed like this, our prior worst underperformance compared with the S&P came in March of 2000, which was a similar environment,” Einhorn said. 
Einhorn cited a value-style strategy, where investors target underperforming, relatively cheap equities, as the main culprit for his January to forget.

Bloomberg reported that Einhorn’s hedge funds posted a decline of 5.5% in January, despite equities broadly catapulting higher for roughly the first six weeks of the year. 
Year-to-date in 2018, one measure of value, the Russell 1000 value index RLV, +0.52% are on pace to decline 0.9% in the first two months of the year, while a comparable fund tracking growth stocks, the Russell 1000 Growth Index RLG, +0.79% is set for a 3.8% return so far in 2018, according to FactSet data. 
Greenlight’s January slump highlights recent struggles for Einhorn, one of the more prominent and well-respected hedge-fund maestros, and many high-profile hedge funds. 
A spokeswoman for Greenlight declined to comment on the hedge fund’s performance. 
Comparatively, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.56% is track for a 4.1% drop in February, while the S&P 500 index SPX, +0.62% is set for a 3.2% decline, even after the main benchmarks (including the Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, +0.92% ) sank 10% from recent peaks about two weeks ago. Last month, the broad-market benchmark rose 5.6%, while the Dow rose 5.8%.
Apparently, the extended woes don’t mean that Einhorn is giving up on his strategy. 
“While the environment has remained difficult with growth stocks accelerating their outperformance against value stocks this year including February, we think a reversion may finally be coming soon,” he said. 
Many investors have complained that a fervor for stocks like Facebook Inc. FB, +2.30% Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.72% Microsoft Corp. MSFT, -0.22% and Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +1.67% among others has driven up so-called growth names, leaving less expensive assets unloved.
